issues.legal_issue: An independent suit whose substance is to invalidate a compromise decree because the compromise was unlawful is barred, even if the plaint frames the requested reliefs as declarations or other forms of relief.
material_facts: A compromise decree had been passed in an earlier suit concerning the property and the plaintiff later brought an independent suit seeking declarations and other reliefs relating to the property and the decree.
The reliefs sought in the later suit could be granted only if the compromise decree were set aside.
The plaintiff had also applied to the court that recorded the compromise to challenge the decree.
issues.conclusion: The independent suit was barred, and the trial court was justified in rejecting the plaint. The reliefs could not avoid the bar merely because they were framed as declarations or other claims.
issues.legal_principle: Order XXIII Rule 3A CPC bars a suit to set aside a decree on the ground that the underlying compromise was unlawful; under the Explanation to Order XXIII Rule 3, a void or voidable compromise is not lawful. The challenge must be made before the court that recorded the compromise. The Court relied on R. Janakiammal v. S.K. Kumarasamy, Banwari Lal v. Chando Devi, Pushpa Devi Bhagat v. Rajinder Singh, R. Rajanna v. S.R. Venkataswamy and Triloki Nath Singh v. Anirudh Singh. It also applied the principle against using clever drafting to disguise a barred claim, relying on T. Arivandandam v. T.V. Satyapal and Ram Singh v. Gram Panchayat Mehal Kalan, among other cases.

predicates.independent_suit_challenges_compromise_d: A plaintiff brings a separate suit seeking relief that challenges a decree made on the basis of a compromise.
predicates.compromise_lawfulness_is_challenged: The plaintiff's claim rests on the contention that the compromise underlying the decree was unlawful.
predicates.requested_reliefs_require_decree_to_be_s: The requested reliefs could not be granted unless the compromise decree were set aside.
predicates.plaint_uses_indirect_reliefs_to_obtain_s: The plaint frames its requests as other kinds of relief but seeks, in substance, the same result as setting aside the compromise decree.

issues.definition: When a separate suit challenges the lawfulness of a compromise decree, it is barred if its requested reliefs depend on setting aside the decree or seek that result indirectly.

issues.legal_issue: When deciding whether to reject a plaint in a suit challenging a compromise decree, the court must address maintainability rather than decide the merits of the decree's validity.
material_facts: The trial court rejected the plaint because it considered the independent suit barred.

The High Court set aside that rejection after considering whether the compromise decree was valid in light of rules concerning compromises made on behalf of a minor, without deciding the bar to the suit.
The plaintiff had already applied to the court that recorded the compromise to challenge the decree, and the validity of the decree remained open for decision in that proceeding.
issues.conclusion: The High Court erred by addressing the merits of the compromise decree instead of deciding whether the independent suit was maintainable. The decree's validity was left for the court that recorded the compromise to decide on the pending application, with the parties' contentions open.
issues.legal_principle: On an application under Order VII Rule 11 CPC, the issue is whether the plaint discloses a maintainable suit, including whether the suit is barred; the court should not determine the merits of the challenged compromise decree at that stage. A challenge to the lawfulness of the compromise is for the court that recorded it under Order XXIII Rule 3. The Court relied on the principles in Banwari Lal v. Chando Devi, Pushpa Devi Bhagat v. Rajinder Singh, R. Rajanna v. S.R. Venkataswamy and R. Janakiammal v. S.K. Kumarasamy.

predicates.application_seeks_plaint_rejection: A party applies for the plaint to be rejected at the threshold.
predicates.suit_challenges_compromise_decree: The suit seeks relief that challenges a decree made on the basis of a compromise.
predicates.court_is_deciding_maintainability: The court is deciding whether the suit can proceed, rather than determining the merits after trial.

issues.definition: When a court considers threshold rejection of a suit challenging a compromise decree, it decides whether the suit may proceed and leaves the decree's validity to the court that recorded the compromise.
